targets.title: Nested two-item/reference window
original_claims: Pass227 reads dy chy taiin shy as a nested construction: dy chy establishes two items and chy taiin shy keeps the second item active across the prescribed value. This combines plural introduction with reference maintenance rather than assigning a new meaning to every token.

original_source_evidence.quote:
# Zweihundertsiebenundzwanzigster Durchgang: kombinierter Werkstattparser

Die Rückkehr- und Doppelungsregeln sind nun in einem gemeinsamen recordweiten Parser verbunden. Er unterscheidet drei Ebenen:

- 381 sichtbare Karten;
- 380 Quelltoken, weil die f82r-Zeilenforttragung zweimal sichtbar, aber einmal gemeint ist;
- 357 Leseeinheiten, davon 343 Einzelkarten und 14 zusammengesetzte Konstruktionen.

Die 14 Konstruktionen tragen 15 Regelanwendungen. Der Unterschied entsteht durch das einzige verschachtelte Fenster `dy chy taiin shy`: `dy chy` setzt zwei Posten, während `chy taiin shy` den zweiten Posten über den Sollwert hinweg aktiv hält.

Der Parser verändert keine Kartenbedeutung. Er erklärt nur, wie ein Schreiber dieselben kleinen Wörter durch Wiederholung und Rahmung zu Mehrzahl, Wiederholung, Rückbezug und Zeilenforttragung zusammensetzen konnte.

Als nächstes wird geprüft, ob diese vier Konstruktionsarten ausreichen, um ein kurzes zusammenhängendes f10r- und f83r-Stück ohne zusätzliche moderne Bindewörter zu übersetzen.

additional_primary_evidence.quote:

targets.assessment: Collapse these three cards into one question. “same stated standard,” “equal/shared/paired,” and “shared reference” are overlapping alternatives, not three independent tests. Equal standard does not entail equal physical amounts; shared reference does not entail both Y tokens denote the same individual; the recipe analogy is explicitly not a reading.
targets.corrected_scope: Ask whether Y–AIIN–Y imposes a relation between two independently identified operands: same standard, shared antecedent/reference, or symmetric/paired value. Keep the three historical cards as rival formulations under one scope.
targets.contrasting_prediction: A discriminating design must include cases with same standard but unequal amounts, distinct operands sharing a standard, and same operand under changed standards. Those outcomes separate standard-sharing, identity/reference, and amount-symmetry models; mere recurrence or two portions does not.
targets.smallest_reopen_input: Freeze two operand endpoints, their amount/standard fields, and antecedent identity independently, then predeclare predictions for standard-sharing, shared-reference, paired-value, and serial/coordinator controls.
targets.source_limit: Historical working/proposal or builder output; no independent manuscript meaning confirmation.

targets.assessment: The V16 table is a confidence-ranked working dictionary row, not an observation. A present portion can be an item or frame-tag in the same contexts, so “Y means portion” is underdetermined by this citation.
targets.corrected_scope: Retain only as a historical lexical proposal; do not use it as evidence for the combined Y–AIIN–Y relation.

targets.smallest_reopen_input: A source-bound sample with independently identified portion, item, unit and frame roles, not a recitation of the V16 table.

targets.assessment: The cited V13 table explicitly reports no number/whole evidence for Part/Share/Partitive and ranks WITH/UNDER SAME REFERENCE first. But WITH can be partitive or relational in context; slot fit and natural German are not decisive.
targets.corrected_scope: Keep whole/part relation, shared reference, coordinator, and generic slot as distinct models; do not call the partitive reading refuted globally.
targets.contrasting_prediction: Partitive predicts a recoverable whole endpoint distinct from the portion; shared-reference predicts one active antecedent without requiring a whole; coordinator predicts two independent operands. original_claims: Keep the latest named plant part, liquid and batch active across physical line ends.

original_source_evidence.quote: 4. Keep the latest named plant part, liquid and batch active across physical

targets.assessment: This is an authored workshop rule (“keep active until explicit continuation changes it”), not a manuscript finding. Physical adjacency/line-end alone cannot establish carryover or an unconditional reset policy.
targets.corrected_scope: Restrict to source-defined line/record transitions and owner changes; preserve carryover, reset-at-boundary, and explicit-continuation models as alternatives.
targets.contrasting_prediction: Carryover predicts the same independently identified plant part/liquid/batch after a physical line end; reset predicts a new/default owner; explicit-continuation predicts carry only when a continuation marker occurs.
targets.smallest_reopen_input: A held set with independently fixed owners on both sides of line ends, including explicit continuation and boundary controls.
